newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius stocks sustained by bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius stocks sustained by bargain hunting.

text.p: The Mauritius bourse share index semdex was down 0.32 points to 305.46 with prices of leading stocks supported by bargain hunting, brokers said.
Transaction volume totalled 5.65 million rupees on 176,839 shares from 10.21 million rupees on 530,656 shares last Friday.
"There were buying orders on some of the blue chip stocks which are presently well undervalued by the market. This limited the slide of the semdex," one dealer said.
The dealer said although the Mauritian bourse was on a downward trend, investors were willing to buy mainly because stocks were fundamentally undervalued by the market.
"But the one-million-dollar question is when will they start buying and what will be the trigger," a dealer said.

Investors were seen as waiting for the Mauritian government to give the right market signal before deciding on any move. Such a signal would include a cabinet reshuffle promised by Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam in August.
Ramgoolam said at the weekend the reshuffle would be made after the country's municipal elections on October 27. This encouraged some buy orders on the leading stocks, dealers said.

Mauritius Commercial Bank rose 50 cents to 70 rupees on 10,930 shares and State Bank of Mauritius was unchanged at 8.50 rupees on 44,500 shares. National Investment Trust rose 60 cents to 10.80 rupees on 2,192 shares and Policy edged up 10 cents to 3.20 rupees on 7,849 shares.
Rogers was unchanged at 81.50 rupees on 6,580 shares and Ireland Blyth gained 10 cents to 11.60 rupees on 3,592 shares.
